rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY (corrected protocol: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-step model.projector swap, bg_target=truth, no fov= override). Hammernik-VN = MRI variational net ported to CT: T untied unrolled steps, each = learned filter-bank + per-filter RBF activation (the _rho_prime bump loop) PLUS an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step (architectural twin of LPD/ItNet but tiny interpretable regulariser). CRITICAL LESSON from the SIBLING hammernik_2017 iter-1: it did NOT diverge to 0.0 -- it CUDA-OOM'd in _rho_prime at 72s with batch_size=4 (16GB RTX5000; the (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF tensors + 5-step autograd blew the card). So the dominant iter-1 risk here is MEMORY, not divergence. MITIGATION: batch_size=2 (NOT 4), vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default -> fewer RBF tensors), vn_checkpoint=true (gradient-checkpoints each unrolled step -- hammernik_vn HAS this knob, cuts activation memory ~T-fold; this is the key difference that lets the projector-in-loop VN fit where the 2017 batch=4 did not). STABILITY against the documented VN family divergence/NaN->0.0 trap: grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY -- the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward; clip_and_step also SKIPS nonfinite-gradient batches so a poisoned step can't collapse the recon to a constant), vn_dc_norm=true (power-iter normalizes R^T(Rx-g) so softplus(lambda_t) stays O(1) regardless of geometry -- the safeguard the projector-less 2017 lacked), lr=5e-4 (the documented hammernik_vn optimum from the discarded run; 8e-4 was worse, brief caps lr<=5e-4), vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 (loose VN-port working-corner hint). CAPACITY conservative per brief: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0 (FBP recon is ~O(1) so the RBF grid [-1,1] covers it). BUDGET: reference -- LPD (projector-in-loop, T=7, ep30, train200, score214) ran 1150s/19.2min right at the edge; hammernik_vn at T=5/N_k=16/checkpointed should be comparable-or-cheaper per step. max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the BINDING constraint (epochs=14 is just an upper bound the wall trips first), leaving ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill. HYPOTHESIS: if I run a budget-sized, MEMORY-SAFE (batch=2, checkpointed), STABLE (grad_clip=1.0, dc_norm) Hammernik-VN, I expect (a) it AVOIDS the hammernik_2017 OOM and produces a FINITE val_ssim within 20min, and (b) the projector DC step lands it near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP SSIM floor -- because a learned-regulariser + true-projector-DC unroll is a sound Mayo recon family (sibling LPD/ItNet/DD-sup all run finite here). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric VN baseline that iter-2+ tunes one knob at a time (epochs/wall first to confirm convergence, then vn_T or vn_lambda_init).
